title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description:
Given a string s, find a longest contiguous substring that reads identically from left to right and from right to left. Return the substring itself, not its length. A substring must use consecutive characters, unlike a subsequence that can skip positions. Comparisons are case-sensitive: uppercase and lowercase letters are distinct. Every one-character substring qualifies.

There may be several equally long answers, so use this precise tie rule: choose the one with the smallest starting index in s. Expanding outward from a center can find both odd-length palindromes (one middle character) and even-length palindromes (a gap between characters). Compare their lengths and their starting positions before updating the winner. A shortcut that tests only odd centers misses strings such as abba.

If the input is empty, return the empty string. The result must appear in the original input with exactly its original spelling. Do not reorder characters or return a reversed copy. For babad, both bab and aba have length three, but the required result is bab because it starts at index zero. Long strings with many repeated letters should not require enumerating every possible substring and separately reversing it.

Example 1:

Input: s = "babad"
Output: "bab"

Example 2:

Input: s = "cbbd"
Output: "bb"

Example 3:

Input: s = ""
Output: ""

Constraints:

  • 0 <= s.length <= 1,000
  • s consists of English letters and decimal digits.
  • On equal lengths return the palindrome with the earliest starting index.
